world.title: Is India a reason behind Egypt staying out of the Mecca Pact?
world.summary: Egypt is considering joining the Saudi-Turkey-Pakistan-led Mecca defence pact, but its participation is uncertain. Riyadh has concerns about Cairo, and Egypt may hesitate to join a bloc that could strain its relations with India and other partners. Historically, India supported Egypt during the 1956 Suez Crisis, highlighting the complexity of Egypt's current geopolitical considerations.

world.title: Indian handle quoted by Netanyahu & US: How a false claim fooled the world
world.summary: A false quote has misled global perceptions regarding Iran's nuclear ambitions, which US President Trump and the Israeli government have cited as justification for military actions against Iran. This narrative has gained traction amidst ongoing peace negotiations. The misinformation highlights the influence of fabricated claims in shaping international relations and public opinion regarding Tehran's alleged nuclear weapons development.

world.title: Who is Natalie Harp, Trump's 'comfort blanket' aide at centre of fresh row?
world.summary: Jon Ossoff raised questions about Natalie Harp's presence during a secretive operation in Turkey with Donald Trump. This incident has sparked increased scrutiny regarding Harp's close relationship with the President and her influential position within his inner circle. Trump's travel companions often indicate his trusted aides, making Harp's involvement particularly noteworthy in the context of this security scare.

business.title: Why Bank of America wants a piece of India's lending boom
business.summary: Bank of America is investing billions in Jio Financial Services Ltd, aiming to capitalize on India's expanding lending market. This strategic move reflects the bank's interest in the country's financial services growth potential. The investment signifies a broader trend of international banks seeking opportunities in India, which is experiencing a significant transformation in its financial landscape and consumer lending.

business.title: Jio Offers Wi-Fi Router with 1500 Square Feet Network Coverage
business.summary: Reliance Jio, India's largest telecom operator, is now providing customers with a Wi-Fi router that offers coverage of up to 1500 square feet. The router is designed to enhance connectivity within homes or offices. Customers are advised to consider factors such as coverage area and supported technology when using the device to maximize its effectiveness.

business.title: Breakout stocks to buy or sell: Sumeet Bagadia recommends five shares to buy today - 18 August 2026
business.summary: Sumeet Bagadia has recommended five breakout stocks to buy: Concord Biotech, Kfin Technologies, KEI Industries, Oberoi Realty, and Finolex Cables. On August 17, the Indian stock market benchmarks, Sensex and Nifty 50, closed lower as investors adopted a cautious stance, focusing on selective sectors and stocks amid better-than-expected Q1FY27 earnings reports.

technology.title: Elden Ring Switch 2 performance improves in new videos, but may fall below 30 fps
technology.summary: Elden Ring's Tarnished Edition is set to release on August 28 for the Switch 2. Recent videos indicate improved performance, but concerns remain regarding frame rates, particularly in handheld mode, where they may drop below 30 fps. Docked mode offers limited enhancements, leaving developers with little time to optimize the game before its upcoming launch.

technology.title: Microsoft admits Windows 11 context menus are sluggish, announces major improvements
technology.summary: Microsoft has acknowledged that context menus in Windows 11 are sluggish and announced significant improvements. The updates will feature enhanced customizability and a streamlined layout, aimed at increasing the speed of opening these menus. These changes will apply to context menus in both File Explorer and the desktop, enhancing user experience and functionality within the operating system.

technology.title: iPhone Ultra leakers reveal new details around release and 'extremely limited' availability
technology.summary: Leaks indicate that Apple's upcoming foldable iPhone, potentially named iPhone Ultra or iPhone Fold, is set for unveiling at the September event. However, its availability at launch is expected to be "extremely limited." The leaks have generated significant interest, but details about specifications and pricing remain scarce as the event approaches. Further information is anticipated soon.

sports.title: 'He’s unbelievable' - Michael Owen tells Man Utd they should have signed £60m Chelsea star Joao Pedro
sports.summary: Michael Owen stated that Manchester United missed an opportunity by not signing Joao Pedro from Watford before his £60 million transfer to Chelsea. He expressed admiration for Pedro's talent and predicted a successful season for Xabi Alonso. Owen, a former striker for Manchester United and Liverpool, believes Pedro could have strengthened the Red Devils' squad significantly.

sports.title: Report: Barcelona’s captaincy order for 2026/27 as two new players enter hierarchy
sports.summary: FC Barcelona winger Raphinha has reportedly been named the first captain for the 2026/27 season. While official confirmation is pending, sources indicate a five-man captaincy group has been established for the upcoming campaign. This change marks a significant shift in leadership, with two new players entering the hierarchy, reflecting the club's evolving structure and future ambitions.

sports.title: Hockey World Cup: ‘Show a bit of composure’ - Fulton’s message to India ahead of must-not-lose Pakistan clash
sports.summary: India head coach Craig Fulton emphasized the need for composure and improved defensive discipline ahead of the crucial match against Pakistan in the Hockey World Cup. Following a 2-4 defeat to England, Fulton highlighted the importance of addressing weaknesses to enhance performance. The team aims to avoid a loss against their rivals, making this match critical for their tournament progression.

health.title: Viral Hepatitis Deaths Increase Worldwide Despite Prevention Efforts
health.summary: Chronic hepatitis B-related deaths rose by 17% since 2015, making up most viral hepatitis fatalities in 2024, according to the 2026 World Health Organization (WHO) Global Hepatitis Report. This increase occurred despite advancements in hepatitis B vaccination and hepatitis C treatment. The report serves as the first assessment of progress in combating viral hepatitis globally.

health.title: AI could bridge the women’s health gap, but better data is the key
health.summary: Women’s health research has been historically underprioritized, leading to significant individual and societal consequences. This neglect affects the predictability of women's health outcomes globally. Experts suggest that artificial intelligence could help address these disparities, but emphasize the necessity for improved data to effectively bridge the gap in women's health. Enhanced data collection is crucial for better research and treatment.

health.title: From the coasts to the plains, bird flu could threaten not just birds - but their homes
health.summary: Australia's bird population, crucial for ecosystems, faces threats from avian influenza. The absence of birds, such as magpies, highlights the impact of the disease on local wildlife. The situation raises concerns about the broader ecological consequences, as birds play essential roles in their habitats. Continued monitoring and research are necessary to understand and mitigate the risks posed by bird flu.

science.title: Cosmic beauty born from a dying star revealed in stunning telescope images
science.summary: NASA's James Webb Telescope has captured stunning images of the Lion Nebula, showcasing its vibrant features. Scientists predict the nebula will disperse in approximately 10,000 years. Within its "mane," researchers have identified hazy, comet-shaped objects, adding to the nebula's cosmic beauty. These new images provide valuable insights for astronomers and excite space enthusiasts and skywatchers alike.

science.title: Pesticides make Argentine ants go crazy, sending them roaming or clustering before workers die
science.summary: Research from UC Riverside reveals that pesticides alter the behavior of Argentine ants, causing increased roaming or clustering before worker ants die. This change in activity does not indicate treatment failure, as the chemicals affect the colony's dynamics. Understanding these behavioral shifts is crucial for effective pest management strategies and interpreting ant activity following pesticide application.

science.title: Labrador Sea a key player in providing oxygen for deep North Atlantic life
science.summary: Researchers from Cornell University have identified the Labrador Sea as a crucial source of oxygen for deep-sea life in the North Atlantic Ocean. Their study, published in Nature Geoscience on August 17, highlights the significance of the churning waters in the region for sustaining marine ecosystems. This discovery enhances understanding of oceanic processes and their impact on deep-sea habitats.

entertainment.title: Sunny Deol says even with Rs 55.99 crore debt when bank issued auction notice for his Juhu home, he was happy: 'I didn’t owe anyone anything, I just had to sell my own assets'
entertainment.summary: Sunny Deol revealed that despite facing a Rs 55.99 crore debt and receiving an auction notice for his Juhu home, he felt content as he owed nothing to anyone. He emphasized that he only needed to sell his own assets. This period of financial struggle preceded the success of 'Gadar 2,' which revitalized his career.

entertainment.title: Anirudh Ravichander and Kavya Maran to marry in Greece? Wedding dates locked for post Diwali - Report
entertainment.summary: Anirudh Ravichander and Kavya Maran are reportedly set to marry in Greece, with wedding dates planned for after Diwali. The speculation surrounding their relationship has intensified, capturing the interest of both entertainment and sports communities. This latest report adds to ongoing rumors about their potential union, although no official confirmation has been provided by either party.

entertainment.title: 'Batwara 1947' box office collection day 4: The Sunny Deol film drops by 72 percent on Monday, struggles to cross Rs 30 crore net while 'Awarapan 2' races ahead towards Rs 100 crore
entertainment.summary: Sunny Deol’s film 'Batwara 1947' experienced a significant drop in box office collections, declining by 72% on its first Monday. The film, which opened with Rs 5.75 crore, struggles to surpass Rs 30 crore net. Meanwhile, 'Awarapan 2' is performing well, moving towards a total of Rs 100 crore. The decline highlights challenges for 'Batwara 1947'.
